notebooks.execution_method: Executed all 35 code cells sequentially from an empty in-process IPython namespace with scripts/execute_notebook_inprocess.py. The final clean run completed in 11.5 seconds, downloaded checksum-tracked Norne inputs from a pinned OPM commit, retained all result-bearing outputs, stored eleven PNG figures, ran a finite-volume reservoir forecast, completed four ES-MDA updates, passed ert lint, and ran three real NeqSim facility cases with zero stored errors or stderr. Retained PNG outputs were then packaged as visually quality-preserving optimized indexed-color PNG files to keep the executed notebook practical for GitHub and Colab; the numerical data and image dimensions were unchanged.

rendered_visual_validation.notes: All eight display equations rendered with correct fractions, Greek symbols, subscripts, superscripts and delimiters. All eleven optimized retained figures were inspected at original resolution after output packaging for labels, units, legends, contrast, scales, clipping, overlap and consistency with stored numerical tables. The dedicated model-setup figure shows the active grid, upscaled net thickness and permeability, wells, imposed controls and flow arrows. The result dashboard shows pressure, oil and water rates, water cut and the water-inventory residual. The final facility plot visibly shows the capacity boundary and the constrained forecast distribution.

known_limitations: The notebook uses published Norne properties and selected published well locations, but educational cell dimensions, vertical upscaling, fluid composition and synthetic observations; it is not a Norne history match or development-decision model.

The portable finite-volume model is executed in every runtime. The full published Norne OPM Flow deck is downloaded and inspected but is not executed because a native Flow binary is not guaranteed in Google Colab.
FMU means Fast Model Update in this notebook, not an FMI Functional Mock-up Unit.
notebooks.issue_handling: No NeqSim defect or actionable API gap was exposed by the executed workflow, so no upstream NeqSim issue was opened. Documentation impact is handled by the examples catalog and this maintenance record.
